text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 7 in history.
1598 - Spanish baroque painter Francisco de Zurbaran born. He became court painter to Philip IV (1638) and was noted for his religious works.

1867 - Marie Curie born as Marie Sklodowska. A Polish-born physicist, she shared the Nobel prize for physics (1903) with her French husband for their work in radioactivity and she won a second Nobel prize for her discovery of radium in 1911.
1872 - The U.S. cargo ship Mary Celeste set sail from New York on a journey which ended when it was found mysteriously abandoned the following month.

1879 - Leon Trotsky born as Lev Davidovich Bronstein. A Russian Communist leader who played a leading role in both the 1905 revolution and the October Revolution in 1917, he was removed from all positions after the death of Lenin in 1924, driven into exile and assassinated in Mexico on August 20, 1940.
1897 - Herman J. Mankiewicz, U.S. screenwriter best known for his Oscar-winning collaboration with Orson Welles in the screenplay of the 1941 film "Citizen Kane", born.
1913 - Albert Camus, Algerian-born French novelist and philosopher, born. Famed for his novels "L'Etranger" (The Outsider) and "La Peste" (The Plague), he won the Nobel prize for literature in 1957.
1917 - Russian Bolsheviks under Lenin overthrew the provisional government of Alexander Kerensky in Petrograd.
1918 - U.S. evangelist Billy Graham born. He made his first crusade in 1949 and travelled throughout the world preaching to huge audiences.
1926 - Dame Joan Sutherland, Australian operatic soprano, born. A coloratura soprano, she became famous with her 1959 appearances in Donizetti's "Lucia di Lammermoor".
1944 - U.S President Franklin D. Roosevelt was re-elected for a record fourth term.
1959 - Victor McLaglen, English-born film actor known for his roles in "Fort Apache", "The Quiet Man", and "The Informer", died.
1962 - Eleanor Roosevelt, wife of President Roosevelt, died. She established the position of first lady and for several years served as a U.S. delegate to the U.N.
1972 - U.S. President Richard Nixon was re-elected for a second term. He became the first president to resign office.
1980 - U.S. film and television actor Steve McQueen died.
1985 - Troops stormed Colombia's Palace of Justice to end a 24-hour siege by gunmen of the M-19 guerrilla movement; 95 people were killed.
1987 - Tunisian President Habib Bourguiba, in office since independence in 1956, was overthrown in a bloodless coup.
1989 - The East German government resigned after pro-democracy protests.
1990 - Mary Robinson was elected in Ireland's first presidential election in 17 years, becoming the country's first woman president.
1992 - Alexander Dubcek, Czech leader who sought to install "socialism with a human face" in the Prague Spring of 1968, died from injuries suffered in a car crash.
